title: Supply-chain risk scan and licensing clarity for model uploads
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Problem: Customers and our review team need clear, machine-readable indicators about what a newly uploaded model allows and what operational constraints exist. Today uploads only include free-text notes and an optional license file; that results in slow manual reviews and missed redistribution/derivative restrictions.

Goal: Implement a lightweight supply-chain risk scan during model ingest that extracts license information, identifies provenance signals for third-party weights, computes a minimal risk score, and surfaces precise, actionable guidance in the Console and the onboarding API. The output must be structured (so downstream automation can gate flows), auditable, and extensible for future checks (cryptographic provenance, training-data claims).

Scope: This ticket covers the product requirements and acceptance criteria for the scanning pipeline and UI/metadata surfaces. Implementation tasks (parsing library, worker, and policy enforcement) are tracked in dependent ENG tickets.
acceptance_criteria: On upload the system returns a structured license verdict with: detected license(s) (SPDX tag if available), confidence level, and an explanation string.
Provenance indicators are produced: origin (model-hub name or upload source), presence of third-party weight artifacts, and SHA256 checksums for large weight files.
A concise risk summary is shown in the Console model details page and available via the onboarding API: risk_level (low|medium|high), user_action_recommended string, and policy_flags list.
Policies can block or require manual review when policy_flags include redistribution_restricted or unknown_license; blocked flows return clear user-facing errors with remediation steps.
All scans are recorded in the model audit timeline with timestamps, scanner version, and links to the raw scan report for compliance audits.
Minimal false-positive rate: manual review of a 200-model stratified sample yields <=8% false-positive flagging for redistribution restrictions.
Console and API surfaces are backward-compatible: existing model metadata endpoints remain stable and include optional new fields.
implementation_notes: Use an open-source SPDX parser (evaluate spdx-tools vs scancode) and normalize results to internal schema.
Worker will checksum weight files >50MB using SHA256 and emit artifact entries; small files remain inline metadata.
Heuristics for third-party weights: presence of common hub URLs, titling patterns ("-weights"), and matching known-vendor fingerprints.
Risk scoring initial factors: license restrictiveness, unknown license confidence, presence of third-party flags, and mismatched provenance claims.
Expose a 'scanner_version' and 'ruleset_hash' in every scan for reproducible audits and future upgrades.
Design will offer three remediation suggestions: (1) provide SPDX license file, (2) add provenance manifest, (3) request legal attestation for encumbered components.
API changes: add optional fields to POST /models/upload response and GET /models/:id; include schema doc in Platform API changelog.
Coordinate with ENG-4122 for the asynchronous scan worker and ENG-5290 for the Console UI panel structure.
This ticket does not enforce legal determinations; it produces signals for review and optional gating by policy.
Plan pilot with 3 internal teams (solutions, enterprise pilot customers) before broad rollout.
Make the scanner opt-out-able for private uploads during the pilot to reduce friction for air-gapped customers.
Create a non-regression test harness with 150 curated model artifacts representing permissive, copyleft, proprietary, and unknown-license cases.
Add telemetry counters: scans_started, scans_failed, flags_emitted_by_type, manual_reviews_created.
Privacy: avoid storing raw training-data metadata; only store derived provenance and checksums necessary for audit trails.
UX copy: avoid legal advice language; provide recommended next steps and links to legal-template artifacts.
Deliverable artifacts: product spec, Console mockups, API schema diff, and pilot onboarding plan.
Estimate: backend parsing + worker (ENG-4122) = 3 sprints; Console + API changes (ENG-5290) = 2 sprints; pilot + iteration = 2 sprints.
Post-launch: schedule quarterly re-scan for models if ruleset or scanner version changes.
Consider future: cryptographic provenance verification (signed manifests) and dataset lineage claims - out of scope for initial rollout.
